input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Deepen flagship league-schedule-generator (allocate.py row 7): the 24-25 team cost item (walk's predecessor scan, a backward table so a move reruns only its own span).

errors.what: Wrote a code comment claiming a 2.4x then 1.6x speed-up for minPlusStep loop variants before measuring; measurement showed the first variant slower and the second ~1.15x.
errors.fix: Dropped the slower variant and rewrote the comment with the measured 0.68-0.77 -> 0.59-0.70 ms before committing.

errors.what: Edited orient.mjs while a benchmark of the 'new' code was running, so its later configurations ran mixed code versions.
errors.fix: Killed it and re-ran the whole new-code benchmark on the final code; only the clean run is reported.

doc_friction.issue: The 'faster break floor' section named a backward table as the fix for the 24-team step; the search's moves span 15 of 23 rounds on average, so the gain was ~15%, not the large cut implied. Recorded in the new section so the next run does not expect more.

carryOverTry is slow (1-11 s for four calls at 9-14 teams); using it to build test timetables made a 48-case equivalence test take 30-39 s. Shuffled circle timetables did the same job in 1 s. Not stated anywhere a test writer would look.

notes: Profile-first: counted 3.48M predecessor scans over 16,828 distinct states on 24 teams seed 1, so balancedWalk caches each state's predecessor list (same order, so the seeded walk is unchanged). floorTable keeps a backward table and trial(lo, hi) reruns only the move's span. minPlusStep branch-free plus lookup permutations. Old vs new page step on 8 leagues (20-25 teams): 1,533 s -> 725 s, identical results/frontier/floor counts in all 8 (eval/backward-table.txt). Venture suite: run_venture_tests.py league-schedule-generator ok (227.6 s) after the walk and backward-table changes; orient + floor-priced tests re-run after the step tweak. 24/25 teams stay off the page (54-184 s). No post-merge real-league check: random leagues only. Local workflows on the final tree: ventures-tests 5/5 (node --test 210.5 s), prompts-ci 2/2, portfolio-validate 100/100, portfolio-pages 8/8 run steps (build steps skipped locally). GitHub reported 0 check runs on the head commit at merge time, so the merge rests on these local runs (CLAUDE.md, 'when runners are starved').

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: profiling, two algorithm changes with equivalence tests, an 8-league old/new benchmark and a write-up, by a senior engineer

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
